what: Per-recording corrections to what the engine is sent (VOICE_DELIVERY.md §7, step 8). Append-only. The line, its display and its spoken text are unchanged, so each recording keeps its id, its key and its place in the site; only the text the engine is given changes. The new take replaces the current file in the results, as the length-check redos did; the replaced takes move to superseded/<stamp>/ and stay. Nothing here generates audio.

corrections.speaker: wataru
corrections.display: …… {辞|や}めさせない ん です か 。
corrections.send: やめさせないんですか。
corrections.decided: Robin, 2026-10-18 (relayed by the local worker): reconcile Wataru's line; the engine input is Cloud's choice, the display unchanged.
why: The reading. 辞 is read や here (the line's own furigana), but on its own it is most often じ (辞書, 辞典). The kana is the reading the line means, sent the way names and seams already are (§7, steps 4-5), so the engine has nothing to guess.

The opening 「……」 is a silent beat, not a sound: the scene shows it, and a line that is only 「……」 is not recorded at all (nonverbal). Wataru's other takes that open with 「……」 run at his ordinary pace (「……何か、分かりましたか。」: 10 morae in 1.78 s), so the engine gives the beat little or no time anyway (judged from the lengths; not listened to here). Leaving it out costs little and removes the one part of the text the engine could stumble on at the very start.

The engine is Wataru's locked Qwen3-TTS reference (a Base model: no style control), so the delivery is carried by the voice and the words alone; nothing else in the send changes. The full stop stays as written.

why: The reading. The line means ふだ (a tablet; its own furigana), but the narrator's engine, AivisSpeech, read the bare kanji as さつ (as in お札, a banknote). Sending the reading for that one word leaves the engine nothing to guess there, the way names and seams are already sent (§7, steps 4-5).

Only the misread word changes. Robin heard nothing else wrong in the take, so the rest of the send stays as it was, kanji included (潮硝子 was read as meant); a whole-line kana send could change a delivery that was fine.

The other eleven wing-10 tablet lines are the same sentence with another place name (「…」の札を拾った。), and 270 more narrator lines mean 札 as ふだ. They were not marked and are not corrected here; they are listed for Robin and the worker (READINESS.md, 2026-10-18).

corrections.sendWas: 言われた通りにしか行かない舟、か。……正直な奴だ。
corrections.send: 言われた通りにしか行かない舟か。……正直な奴だ。
changes: the comma before か left out
corrections.decided: Robin, 2026-10-18, listening decisions (relayed by the local worker; the decisions file is kept locally): redo; 'The overall delivery is good, except the か with a strange delay likely caused from the comma.'
why: The pause. In the line the comma marks a reflective beat (a barge, one that only goes where it is told), but the engine made it a stop inside the phrase, so the か that closes the thought arrives late. Without the comma the engine says 舟か as one phrase; the 「……」 before the second sentence stays, so the line keeps its turn.
Only the comma changes. Robin found the delivery otherwise good, so the words, their kanji and the rest of the punctuation stay as they were; the display keeps its comma.
A send correction may leave out a comma, as SC1 left out a silent opening beat; the words and their reading never change (VOICE_DELIVERY.md §7, step 8).

corrections.speaker: narrator
corrections.decided: Robin, 2026-10-18, review round 3 (relayed by the local worker; 12 redo, 21 keep): redo; 'should read as Shi-o-do-ma-ri but is heard as Sho-do-ma-ri - focus on the kana size'.
why: The beats. The word is し・お・ど・ま・り, five morae with お a beat of its own; the narrator's engine, AivisSpeech, runs しお together into one syllable, しょ, so Robin hears shodomari. The same reading in katakana, シオドマリ, kept the five beats in the worker's trials: the local recognizer heard しおどまり in 4 of 6 takes, against 1 of 6 for the hiragana and 1 of 6 for the kanji.

Only the script changes. The word and its reading stay: katakana writes the same sounds, so this is the reading in kana (VOICE_DELIVERY.md §7, step 8, which now says so). The trials with commas (しお、どまり 0 of 6; し、お、ど、ま、り 0 of 6) would add pauses the word does not have, and did worse.

A reference reading has no line: what the game shows is the word and its reading. The key, the written word, the reading and spoken do not change, so the id and the word's place in the site's reference index stay.
